results.title: [PDF] what the Draw-A-Scientist Test shows science undergraduate ...
results.content: Vol.:(0123456789) Discover Education (2024) 3:263 | https://doi.org/10.1007/s44217-024-00365-7 Discover Education Research Dr Boring: what the Draw‑A‑Scientist Test shows science undergraduate students think about scientists Vanessa Crump1 Received: 28 August 2024 / Accepted: 22 November 2024 © The Author(s) 2024 OPEN Abstract This study sought to determine what undergraduate science students envision when asked to picture a scientist at work. The Draw-A-Scientist Test (DAST) and variations have been used over 40 years to explore student perceptions of scientists. Although 42% of female students drew female scientists and incorporated more non-stereotypical elements, most students lacked a robust self-image as scientists. Despite the evidence that respondents’ perceptions of scientists do not reflect reality [7], the stereotypical image of a scientist as a nerdy, boring male, white, wearing a lab coat and working alone indoors in a glassware-filled laboratory is persistent and pervasive across different demographics and nationalities [7–13], and even among scientists [14]. 1.1  The development of the Draw‑A‑Scientist Test Chambers [21] developed the well-known Draw-A-Scientist Test (DAST) to investigate primary students’ perceptions of scientists and their work.
